title.narrative: Indicator 3.2 Number of exchange visits between Libyan municipalities

description.narrative: Indicator 3.2 Number of exchange visits between Libyan municipalities

comment.narrative: The value inputed is the cumulative value since the beninning of the project. During the reporting period 8 exchange visits took place. Comment This includes meetings that were conducted during the fishery pilot project field visit to Libya October 2022 and March 2023 where Libyan Municipalities representatives had the opportunity to meet other partner Municipalities in Tripoli Zliten Benghazi and Tobruk. Moreover exchange visits were autonomously jointly organised by the University and Municipality staff during the delivery of the inpresence training in the Municipalities by University Trainers. The exchange visits involved both target and nontarget Municipalities In June 2022 during the Cycle 1 training the municipality of Beni Walid organised a meeting with the municipality of Derna in order to benefit from their experience in the field of urban planning. Case studies were presented to enrich the course with different experiences. Moreover during Cycle 2 training in Municipalities Beni Walid Municipality visited Zliten Municipality and the Beni Walid Social Security Fund During Cycle 2 Zintan visited Jadu Municipality and staff members of the Municipalities of AlRayina Jadu AlQurayyat attended the training in Zintan. Exchange visits took place between partners from Benghazi and Sebha municipalities at no cost for the project as well as from Benghazi and Beni Walid namely on sharing the experience of the Benghazi Urban Observatory.Finally it should be noted that during Year 2 the number of online meetings and informal exchanges among partners and external actors has increased dramatically which signals the start of the development of the community of practice.

comment.narrative: At the onset of the project target municipalities have very poor knowledge of the level of satisfaction of services by their citizens and do not use robust evaluation methods to assess this.

By the end of the project Municipalities will have acquired new competencies that will have allow them to assess the level of satisfaction of their citizens and will have stronger knowledge about the gaps and needs for service provision.

The indicator is updated on the bases of the interviews conducted with the Project Managers and other relevant parties involved in the preparation of the Local Development Plans and on the analysis of the methodologies used to prepare the said Plans.It is the PMUs intention to suggest deleting this indicator through an amendment because it is not measurable with the current budget.During 2023 it was possible to assess that in developing the Local Development Plans most of the Municipalities adopted a bottomup approach but few relied solely on local notables technical experts and business elites to set the priorities for each sector. When it comes to stakeholders outreaching not all municipalities succeeded in involving a wider sector of the society such as civil society women youth and people with special needs and some municipalities have limited outreaching capacity which hindered their capacity to attract support from international organisations.

title.narrative: 1. A human rightsbased training curriculum for Libyan municipalities is validated.grants and other vulnerable workersces)

description.narrative: There are two steps in the process of curriculum validation: The first step is the adoption of the training curriculum by the Municipalities after it has been piloted (which implies obtaining feedback on content, methodology, approach, etc., integrating suggestions, and achieving consensus among municipalities on the final version of the curriculum itself). The second step is the validation of the curriculum by authorities at central level, which gives more credibility and strength to curriculum. The first step is the real output of the Project, while the second step (which takes more time and depends on national politics, i.e., elements outside the projects control) pertains to the impact of the project.

title.narrative: Indicator 1.3 Degree of integration of equal opportunities and gender equality within the training modules of the curriculum

description.narrative: The expected training curriculum is based on 6 cycles (each including 3 thematic modules). The indicator assesses to what extent equal opportunities and gender equality are mainstreamed in the modules content.

comment.narrative: At the onset of the project no curriculum tackling equal opportunities and gender equality is really available for Municipalities.
By the end of the project all validated curricula integrate equal opportunities and gender equality to a significant degree as evaluated through an objective evaluation grid.
